item.title: Photoemission study of Iodoalkanes
item.description: arXiv:2610.19055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Core level atomic photoionization is influenced by the molecular environment of the emitting atom. To probe this influence we used extreme ultraviolet (XUV) radiation to measure the I$\left(4d\to\varepsilon f \right)$ photoemission of four iodine substituted alkanes in the range from 60 eV to 160 eV photon energy. Using two detection angles relative to light polarization allowed us to extract and compare the asymmetry parameter of the investigated compounds. These results are in agreement with theory by Pi and Landsman (L.-W. Pi and A. Landsman, Attosecond time delay in photoionization of noble-gas and halogen atoms, Applied Sciences 8, 322 (2018)) and previous experiments by Olney et al. (T. N. Olney, G. Cooper, and C. Brion, Quantitative studies of the photoabsorption (4.5-488 ev) and photoionization (9-59.5 ev) of methyl iodide using dipole electron impact techniques, Chemical Physics 232, 211 (1998)) for iodomethane. 2-iodopropane behaves nearly identical to iodomethane, while for iodoethane and 1-iodopropane we find a distinct and consistent, energy dependant difference most prominent at around 130 eV photon energy. This further proves the influence of the chemical environment on core level photoionization. Due to the sensitivity on the exact positions of the carbon atoms and the energy dependence we hypothesise this difference is caused by intramolecular scattering of the outgoing photoelectron wave packet, causing changes in the angular distribution.
item.dc:creator: Maximilian Forster, Maximilian Pollanka, Sven-Joachim Paul, Pascal Freisinger, Christian Schr\"oder, Robert Richter, Michele Alagia, Alessio Bruno, Stefano Stranges, Reinhard Kienberger

item.title: Wigner time delay in the $4d$ giant-resonance region of iodoalkanes
item.description: arXiv:2610.19402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The iodine $4d$ giant resonance provides an unusually strong and predominantly iodine-centered photoionization channel in iodoalkanes. Recent attosecond measurements by Schr\"oder et al. [Phys. Rev. A 112, L051104 (2025)] reported pronounced, nonmonotonic, and isomer-dependent variations of the streaking-derived $4d$ photoemission delay across the molecular series. We calculate field-free molecular Eisenbud--Wigner--Smith (EWS) delays from photoionization amplitudes represented in a multicenter B-spline basis of the time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT). A tensor formulation is developed in which the delay for randomly oriented molecules is evaluated from the same rank-0 and rank-2 contractions that determine the cross section and anisotropy parameter. The resulting TDDFT delays of CH$_3$I, C$_2$H$_5$I, 2-iodopropane, and both calculated conformers of 1-iodopropane form a narrow bundle throughout the 90--118~eV region and closely follow atomic-I and I$^-$ reference calculations. This robustness is consistent with the similarly weak molecular dependence of the giant resonance cross section and angular distribution, but it is in marked contrast with the much larger molecular variation found by streaking experiments. The asymptotic Coulomb--laser-coupling/continuum--continuum correction is controlled mainly by the photoelectron energy and residual charge and is therefore expected to be nearly common to the iodoalkane series. This does not exclude target-specific molecular IR effects beyond the universal Coulomb term.
item.dc:creator: Anatoli S. Kheifets, Daniele Toffoli, Piero Decleva

item.title: Fine-structure Raman interferometry with metastable barium for magnetically resilient inertial sensing
item.description: arXiv:2610.20168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Atom-interferometric quantum inertial sensors are promising candidates for inertial navigation systems owing to their high sensitivity and intrinsically low drift. However, their application to next-generation inertial navigation, targeting a drift below 100 m/month, requires exceptionally stringent inertial-sensor bias stability. In conventional Raman atom interferometers based on ground-state hyperfine transitions, suppressing inertial-sensor biases arising from quadratic Zeeman shifts requires highly optimized magnetic shielding. In this work, we propose a Raman atom interferometer based on fine-structure transitions between metastable states of barium, which exhibit a quadratic Zeeman sensitivity approximately three orders of magnitude lower than that of conventional alkali-atom Raman transitions. We show that the proposed scheme increases the allowable spatial gradient of the magnetic-field magnitude by a factor of several tens, thereby relaxing the magnetic-field-control requirements from highly optimized shielding and compensation systems to standard magnetic-field-control techniques. Furthermore, we experimentally demonstrate Mach--Zehnder interference between metastable fine-structure states of barium, validating a key building block of the proposed inertial-sensing scheme.

item.title: Demonstration of a mobile ion-trap quantum device
item.description: arXiv:2610.20487v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Trapped-ion devices are being investigated for transportable applications, including the transfer of exotic charged particles between laboratories and the development of portable quantum technologies. To date, ion transport has been demonstrated only in magnetic (Penning) traps, whereas radiofrequency (Paul) traps are the predominant platform in quantum science. Here, we report the first transport of a few thousand ions confined in a linear Paul trap over distances of several kilometers, with transport durations of 15 and 45 min. These results establish a foundation for mobile trapped-ion quantum devices capable of operating while in motion and may enable the transport of exotic ions in Paul traps between experimental facilities.
item.dc:creator: Sara Alfaro, Dipesh Bhanushali, Sankarshan Choudapurkar, Ashwin Bhartia, Thomas Lafenthaler, Tommaso Faorlin, Yannick Weiser, Lorenz Panzl, Thomas Monz, Rainer Blatt, Giovanni Cerchiari

item.title: Structured-Light Magnetometry in a Coherently Controlled Atomic Medium
item.description: arXiv:2603.25781v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A structured-light-based approach to magneto-optical rotation (MOR) magnetometry is proposed, in which magnetically induced polarization rotation is converted into a directly observable spatial displacement. A radially polarized Laguerre--Gaussian beam propagating through cold $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$ atoms in the presence of a longitudinal magnetic field experiences circular birefringence, which induces a relative phase shift between the $\sigma_+$ and $\sigma_-$ polarization components. This phase shift manifests itself as the angular rotation of a petal-shaped interference pattern, enabling the MOR angle to be determined directly from the spatial intensity distribution. Unlike conventional MOR detection techniques based on balanced polarimetry or Stokes-parameter reconstruction, the proposed method requires only a fixed-axis polarization projection and avoids computationally intensive polarization analysis. By translating polarization rotation into a topology-dependent spatial observable, the scheme enables direct and spatially resolved magnetic-field measurements. Furthermore, the use of electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) allows low-loss operation while preserving high sensitivity. These characteristics make the proposed technique a promising platform for optical magnetometry and structured-light-based quantum sensing.
item.dc:creator: Parkhi Bhardwaj, Shubhrangshu Dasgupta

item.title: Resonant photoionization dynamics during optical trapping of lithium atoms
item.description: arXiv:2608.09549v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Photoionization induced by trapping and auxiliary laser fields is an inherent feature of many laser-cooling and optical trapping experiments, yet its microscopic dynamics are rarely investigated directly. In this work, we employ a reaction microscope implementing an event-by-event photoionization time retrieval technique to extend momentum-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy to continuous-wave laser--atom interactions. We investigate low-intensity multicolor photoionization of laser-cooled lithium atoms confined in an all-optical trap. Complete three-dimensional electron momentum distributions and kinetic-energy spectra recorded for different laser wavelengths and polarization configurations identify resonant excitation of the $5p$ and $5f$ states and reveal an additional ionization channel following spontaneous decay from the $5f$ to the $4d$ state. A pronounced polarization dependence of the photoionization yield is explained by magnetic-sublevel selection rules and the coherent interference of different virtual excitation pathways. These results demonstrate that reaction microscopy combined with event-by-event time reconstruction provides a powerful approach for investigating microscopic electronic dynamics in laser-cooled atomic systems and offers new insight into photoionization processes occurring during optical trapping.
item.dc:creator: K. Foster, S. Majumdar, D. Fischer

item.title: An Aubry-Andr\'e localized optical lattice clock
item.description: arXiv:2610.17499v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Optical lattice clocks in space could improve satellite navigation systems and enable new tests of fundamental physics, including gravitational-wave detection and tests of relativity. In microgravity, atoms can tunnel to degenerate neighboring lattice sites, broadening the clock transition and limiting coherence times. We demonstrate Aubry-Andr\'e localization in a bichromatic optical lattice formed by two magic-wavelength lasers, suppressing tunneling in a horizontal lattice clock emulating free fall. We recover a Fourier-limited clock Rabi spectrum and measure Ramsey coherence times of up to 2 s in shallow lattices, with up to 100-fold improvement over the delocalized regime. These results establish Aubry-Andr\'e localization as a practical route to controlling tunneling in future space-based clocks, and open a path to operating terrestrial clocks at shallower lattice depths.
item.dc:creator: Shuo Ma, Anke St\"oltzel, Bennett Christensen, Zhuoli Ding, Dhruva Ganapathy, Andrew Householder, Genyue Liu, Shimon Kolkowitz

item.title: Critical properties of bound states with one-boson-exchange potential
item.description: arXiv:2510.10420v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this study, we discuss some general critical properties of bound states with one-boson-exchange potential. For simplicity, we first take a system with two identical scalar particles as an example. The interaction between these two scalar particles is described by the exchange of another massive scalar meson under the instantaneous approximation, which results in the Yukawa potential. A highly accurate numerical method is used to determine the critical mass value of the system. The resulting critical mass for the ground state is consistent with those reported in the literature, agreeing to about 35 significant figures. The highly accurate results for the $l=1$ case are also presented, which are significantly more precise than those previously reported in the literature. Furthermore, we extend the discussion to physical hadronic molecular states, where form factors are introduced in the interaction to describe the structure of hadrons. Our numerical results show that although the binding energies of the hadronic molecular states depend on the cutoff in the form factors, the number of hadronic molecular states is almost independent of the cutoffs across a very wide physical region. This indicates a strong and important property: for physically small couplings, the number of hadronic molecular states is almost solely determined by the coupling constants and the masses of the exchange particles. This highly accurate numerical method can also be straightforwardly applied to higher $l$ cases or other systems.
item.dc:creator: Lin-Qing Song, Hai-Qing Zhou

item.title: Heterogeneous entanglement between a trapped ion and a solid-state quantum memory
item.description: arXiv:2603.05836v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hybrid quantum networks offer a promising architecture for scalable quantum information processing and a future quantum internet, as they can combine the complementary strengths of disparate physical platforms. While single-atom systems provide deterministic quantum logic gates, atomic ensembles enable large-capacity quantum storage. However, generating entanglement between such heterogeneous systems has remained an open challenge, primarily due to fundamental spectral mismatches and system complexity. Here, we demonstrate a hybrid quantum network that entangles a single trapped $\mathrm{^{171}Yb^{+}}$ ion and a quantum memory based on $\rm ^{153}Eu^{3+}\colon\!Y_2SiO_5$ crystal over a 75-m separation. Using polarization-maintaining quantum frequency conversion, we map spin-photon entanglement onto a hybrid entanglement between a single spin qubit and a collective excitation of the quantum memory. The resulting entangled state achieves a fidelity of $(89.21 \pm 2.23)\%$ and violates the CHSH-Bell inequality by 6 standard deviations ($S = 2.328 \pm 0.055$), confirming nonlocality between two heterogeneous nodes. This work establishes entanglement between a quantum processing module with a multiplexed quantum memory node, representing a key step toward a scalable, multifunctional quantum internet.
